candidateSource.backendChange: Router sends B preparation then one A preparation-and-execution request; A creates its readiness receipt inside its existing wallet DO.

method: Three fresh implicit, unfunded NEAR wallets in each sequential baseline, combined A preparation/execution, and restored control arm. The same SDK and client machine run all arms. Only Router and Deriver A versions change. B, Signing Worker, Console, Gateway and placement settings stay fixed.

structuralSavings.scope: Preparation and execution requests only. D1 counters cover the bound-root subset.

localVerification.scope: Real local Workers, D1, Durable Objects, protocol execution, and persistence. No cryptographic primitive or SDK code changed.
localVerification.testUpdate: The removed A preparation endpoint no longer returns a receipt to Router. Relocation verification reads the genuine persisted A receipt. Retirement holds B admission before the combined A request.

independentSignatureVerification.verifier: Node.js crypto Ed25519 with independent NEP-413 Borsh encoding

limitations: Three samples per arm do not establish tail percentiles or a latency guarantee.
Sequential arms include provider scheduling and network variation.
Fresh wallets do not prove cold Workers. Worker cold starts were not controlled.
Invocation wall time can include background work and is not browser response time.
Nested spans overlap. Protocol spans include transport. Concurrent status durations must not be added.
Bound-root D1 counters cover a subset of database work. Total registration D1 calls remain unmeasured.
The candidate serializes A admission behind B preparation while removing A preparation HTTP and DO requests. D1 freshness checks remain.
Requested APAC placement does not prove physical colocation.

decision.reason: One Router-to-A request and one A Worker-to-DO request per ceremony are removed. The obsolete A preparation endpoint is deleted. All nine local Worker/DO scenarios and nine hosted independently verified signatures pass.
decision.userDirection: Keep correct, simple optimizations that analytically reduce work or network requests despite small-sample timing variation. Record structural savings separately from measured latency and compare cumulative changes later.
decision.tradeoff: A root admission now follows B preparation. This serial work measured 147–204 ms, median 155 ms. D1 round trips and SQL statement counts did not fall.
decision.uncertainty: One sequential three-sample comparison cannot isolate the candidate effect from provider and network variation. The slower candidate must remain visible; it is not established as provider-only noise.
decision.nextStep: Target the remaining A-to-B connection and forwarding boundaries. Keep independent role checks. Compare the accumulated accepted changes against a frozen earlier baseline, and reconsider serialization if repeated measurements show a material regression.
